lessons_learned: Lessons learned should include both positive and negative experiences to improve work processes, equipment design, operation, quality, safety, and cost effectiveness.
Performance measures for lessons learned programs should focus on how well the program uses opportunities to develop lessons, the quality of the lessons created, and integration into improvements.

The lessons learned infrastructure should use existing systems where possible, and clearly defined ownership should be established for maintaining the infrastructure and support for development, communication, and use.
Mechanisms for identifying potential lessons learned should be simple in terms of volume, type of information, and input mechanisms.
Lessons should be context-driven, with information defined in terms of the environment in which they were learned and their significance.
There should be no stigma or blame assigned to individuals who identify a lesson learned.
The objective of lessons learned programs is to provide a means of communicating experiences that can reduce risk, improve efficiency, and enhance cost effectiveness of processes and operations.
Lessons learned should be disseminated with an assigned priority descriptor indicating the risk, immediacy, and urgency of the content.
Priority descriptors for lessons learned include Red (>$35K USD), Blue ($5K-$35K USD), Green (<$5K USD), and Yellow (Good Practice).
Lessons learned documents for local use may be tailored as appropriate for local needs but should include enough metadata to identify and determine their relevance within the company and departments.
